scope: Continuing original RC18 and RC30/31 read-only overlays; 15 records for seven sparse priority species
policy: No status imputed across assessment authorities. Global versus national separate. Samples do not imply current site occupancy. A morphological contrast may require animal-specific scale examination. Owner permissions and photographic rights separately assessed before packaging.

records.label: North Mindoro forest mosaic observations
records.text: Eleven-year observation records describe Bangon Monitor Lizards within a privately monitored secondary tropical lowland forest mosaic in Abra de Ilog, Occidental Mindoro, including areas of partly closed canopy.
records.sourceLocation: Study area, Munting Buhangin site description, pp. 2–3
records.studyScope: Local site context, not a comparison of preferred habitats or a regional occupancy model.

records.label: Abra de Ilog study locality
records.text: Observers recorded Bangon Monitor Lizards in the municipality of Abra de Ilog, northern Occidental Mindoro, across an observation period from 2011 through 2022.
records.studyScope: Historical regional observation records; not a confirmed current detection at a user's GPS station.

records.label: Recorded cane-toad feeding
records.text: The Abra de Ilog study documented Bangon Monitor Lizards consuming invasive cane toads and reported observations of juveniles feeding on insects.
records.studyScope: Recorded prey in local individuals, not an experimentally tested general toxin immunity or full seasonal diet.

records.label: Local trapping and exploitation reports
records.text: The 2023 Mindoro study documents local trapping of water monitors and reports that the authors destroyed more than thirty snares in the studied area during 2022.
records.studyScope: Local threats and enforcement observations, not a nationwide population decline estimate.

records.label: Global and Philippine categories remain distinct
records.text: The IUCN SSC Monitor Lizard Specialist Group summarizes a 2021 global Least Concern assessment and a separate Philippine DENR 2019-09 Category D listing for Varanus bangonorum.
records.source: IUCN SSC Monitor Lizard Specialist Group (n.d.), Varanus bangonorum
records.sourceLocation: Red List Status and National Protection, both dated source summaries
records.studyScope: Secondary specialist-group account. The global LC category has 2021 assessment edition; the national category is a separate 2019 listing. Verify exact official primary entries before marking legal-source complete.

records.label: Stream-bank boulder records in northeast Mindanao
records.text: The 2016 northeast Mindanao herpetofauna survey collected Cyrtodactylus agusanensis among boulders along stream banks at surveyed eastern Mindanao sites.
records.sourceLocation: Family Gekkonidae, Cyrtodactylus agusanensis species account
records.studyScope: Observed microhabitat of sampled animals. Not a prediction that all streams contain the gecko or a proof of obligate dependence.

records.label: Range narrowed after the 2010 species complex revision
records.text: The northeast Mindanao survey reports Cyrtodactylus agusanensis from eastern Mindanao under the taxonomic treatment revised in 2010, not from the entire older Mindanao–Leyte–Dinagat species complex.
records.sourceLocation: Cyrtodactylus agusanensis species treatment and references to Welton et al. 2010
records.studyScope: Scope follows the revised species concept. Historical records assigned to the broader complex require checking; not a site occupancy assertion.

records.label: Differential scale counts against C. gubaot
records.text: The 2010 revision distinguishes C. agusanensis from C. gubaot by sampled midbody dorsal scales (111–124 versus 92–105), paravertebral scales (184–196 versus 150–162), and postcloacal lateral tubercles (8–11 versus 4–6).
records.sourceLocation: Comparative diagnosis of Cyrtodactylus gubaot against C. agusanensis
records.studyScope: Counts reflect analyzed specimen material and need examination; photographs with no reliable scale detail cannot substitute for diagnosis.

records.label: Agusan Marsh disturbance-edge records
records.text: A 2026 inventory recorded Philippine Box Turtles in disturbed and cultivated areas adjacent to the freshwater swamp forest of Agusan Marsh.
records.studyScope: Specific regional observations, not a quantified habitat preference or evidence of tolerance at all Philippine sites.

records.label: Reviewed Agusan Marsh specimens
records.text: The 2026 Agusan Marsh study reported a Philippine Box Turtle from Rosario, Agusan del Sur and another salvaged specimen from Talacogon, documenting two regional records.
records.sourceLocation: Cuora philippinensis species treatment, Material examined (BIRC 774, MBS 2208)
records.studyScope: Two specimens and historical/collected material; no current station detection or complete national range model.

records.label: Head stripe and shell characters in Agusan Marsh series
records.text: The Philippine Box Turtle treatment describes a vertebrally keeled carapace, nearly black adult plastron, and a yellow stripe running from the snout through the upper orbital region.
records.sourceLocation: Cuora philippinensis, Identification, reference to Taylor and Diesmos studies
records.studyScope: Characters described for the study and earlier treatments. New taxonomic split from Cuora amboinensis means similar box-turtle forms require careful current taxonomy.

records.label: Adult and juvenile distinctions from other king cobras
records.text: The 2024 king-cobra revision diagnoses Luzon Ophiophagus salvatana adults by the absence of pale body bands; juveniles have about 85–86 sharply angled pale bands, versus 27–48 for the compared O. hannah and O. kaalinga.
records.source: Das et al. (2024), European Journal of Taxonomy 961:1–51
records.sourceLocation: Ophiophagus salvatana original species diagnosis, pp. 30–34
records.studyScope: Use sex and age appropriate characters from examined specimens. Juvenile band pattern alone and island context do not establish identity; no handling or close approach is implied.

records.label: Luzon type-series provenance
records.text: The 2024 description of Ophiophagus salvatana used a Luzon holotype from Baguio and comparative Luzon specimens including Camarines Sur, Isabela and Pampanga.
records.source: Das et al. (2024), European Journal of Taxonomy 961:1–51
records.studyScope: Published specimen localities and historic identifications only; not a complete current occurrence map.

records.label: Philippine national Critically Endangered record
records.text: The Philippine Department of Environment and Natural Resources identifies Dinagat hairy-tailed cloud rat Crateromys australis as Critically Endangered in its national threatened-species discussion.
records.source: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (n.d.), cloud rat conservation notice
records.sourceLocation: DENR-NCR cloud rat conservation notice, national threatened-fauna categorization
records.studyScope: Government secondary explanation linked to the national list. The notice refers to Administrative Order 2019-19 in error; the governing fauna list is 2019-09, so verify the source order separately. This is not an IUCN category.

records.label: Philippine national Critically Endangered listing
records.text: Dugong dugon appears in the Critically Endangered mammals category of the Philippine Department of Environment and Natural Resources 2019-09 threatened-fauna list.
records.source: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (2019), DAO 2019-09
records.sourceLocation: Section 3, Category A Critically Endangered, Mammals, Dugongidae
records.studyScope: Dated Philippine national classification only, not the global IUCN category or a modern population estimate.
